records.issue_text: embeddable-host.js.es6 destroyRecord() has no .catch, so a failed delete leaves the row in place with an unhandled promise rejection and no user feedback
records.rationale: The diff confirms the asymmetry: in embeddable-host.js.es6 the save action has `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, while the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`, so a failed server-side delete (e.g., 422/500) silently leaves the host record in the store with an unhandled rejection and no user feedback. This is a concrete robustness gap in newly added code, not a defect in normal-path behavior.

records.issue_text: rest.js.es6 uses type.replace('_', '-') without the /g flag, replacing only the first underscore, so admin models with two or more underscores won't match ADMIN_MODELS and get routed to the non-admin path
records.rationale: The diff shows `if (ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-')) !== -1)` in rest.js.es6, and JS replace without /g only substitutes the first occurrence, so a model like 'some_admin_thing' would become 'some-admin_thing' and fail to match ADMIN_MODELS. The mechanism is real and verifiable, but no current entry ('plugin', 'site-customization', 'embeddable-host' via 'embeddable_host') has more than one underscore, so no existing behavior is broken — a concrete latent routing risk for future admin models rather than a defect today.
records.stripped_text: rest.js.es6 uses type.replace('_', '-') without the /g flag, replacing only the first underscore, so admin models with two or more underscores won't match ADMIN_MODELS and get routed to the non-admin path

records.issue_text: store.js.es6 'hydrated || []' is dead code since map always returns an array
records.rationale: The diff shows `const hydrated = obj[k].map(function(id) {...}); obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [];`. Since Array.prototype.map always returns an array (truthy even when empty), `|| []` is indeed unreachable dead code. However, this is purely cosmetic with zero behavioral effect — a style nit, not a defect or substantive advisory.
